questions.question: Lokesh travels from City A to City B. If Lokesh drives his car at 3/4 of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 24 minutes late.Find the time (in minutes) that Lokesh would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio = 3 : 4 (New : Normal)

Time ratio = 4 : 3 (New : Normal) [Since distance is constant]

Difference in time ratio = 4 − 3 = 1 part.

1 part = 24 minutes.

Normal time = 3 parts = 3 × 24 = 72 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 72 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New speed = 3/4 of normal speed.

Time delayed = 24 minutes.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 
• 
 
 
 City A
 
 
 City B
 
 

 

 Normal Speed = S | Time = T
 
 

 

 New Speed = 3/4 S | Time = T + 24
 
 Distance is Constant

**Calculations:**

Let the normal speed be S and normal time be T.

⇒ Normal distance = S × T

⇒ New speed = 3S / 4

⇒ New time = T + 24

Since the distance between City A and City B is constant:

⇒ S × T = (3S / 4) × (T + 24)

⇒ T = 3/4 × (T + 24)

⇒ 4T = 3(T + 24)

⇒ 4T = 3T + 72

⇒ 4T − 3T = 72

⇒ T = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional (S ∝ 1/T). If the ratio of speeds is a : b, then the ratio of the corresponding times will be b : a.

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When an object travels two equal distances at speeds S₁ and S₂, the Average Speed over the entire journey is given by (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

If two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is S₁ − S₂. If they are moving in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂.
</p

questions.question: A can finish a work in 16 days, and B can do the same work in 12 days. While with the help of C, they completed the work in 4 days. in how many days can C alone do the same work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(16, 12, 4) = 48 units.

Efficiency of A = 48 ÷ 16 = 3 units/day, B = 48 ÷ 12 = 4 units/day.

Combined efficiency of (A + B + C) = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 units/day.

Efficiency of C = 12 − (3 + 4) = 5 units/day.

Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 48/5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 48/5 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 16 days

Time taken by B = 12 days

Time taken by A, B, and C together = 4 days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A

 48 ÷ 16 = 3
 
 

 B
 12
 48 ÷ 12 = 4
 
 

 A + B + C
 4
 48 ÷ 4 = 12
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of A + B + C = 12 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = Total Efficiency − (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 12 − (3 + 4)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 12 − 7 = 5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 48 ÷ 5 days

**∴ The correct answer is 48/5 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the work done. If individuals work for the same number of days, their wages are divided exactly in the ratio of their daily efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The mathematical concept is identical to Time and Work, with the key difference that an emptying pipe or leak is considered to have a negative efficiency.

Alternate Day Work

When people work on alternate days, find the total work completed in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people). Then multiply by the maximum possible integer cycles before manually completing the remaining fractional work.
</p

questions.question: The average weight of Shivam, Rupesh and Mandar is 46 kg. If the average weight of Shivam and Rupesh be 39 kg and that of Rupesh and Mandar be 48 kg, then the weight of Rupesh (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight = Average × Number of people

Weight of Rupesh = (Sum of S and R) + (Sum of R and M) − (Sum of S, R and M)

Weight of Rupesh = (39 × 2) + (48 × 2) − (46 × 3)

Weight of Rupesh = 78 + 96 − 138

Weight of Rupesh = 174 − 138 = 36 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 36 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of Shivam, Rupesh and Mandar = 46 kg

Average weight of Shivam and Rupesh = 39 kg

Average weight of Rupesh and Mandar = 48 kg

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 
 Shivam (S)
 
 
 Rupesh (R)
 
 
 Mandar (M)

 

 Total S + R + M = 138 kg

 

 S + R = 78 kg

 

 R + M = 96 kg

 
• 
 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of S, R and M = 46 × 3 = 138 kg

⇒ Total weight of S and R = 39 × 2 = 78 kg

⇒ Total weight of R and M = 48 × 2 = 96 kg

⇒ We can see that by adding the two smaller sets, Rupesh's weight is counted twice:

⇒ (S + R) + (R + M) = 78 + 96

⇒ S + 2R + M = 174 kg

⇒ Now, subtract the total weight of all three from this sum to find the overlap (Rupesh):

⇒ R = (S + 2R + M) − (S + R + M)

⇒ R = 174 − 138 = 36 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 36 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average = Sum of all values ÷ Total number of values.

Overlapping Set Concept

When subsets of a whole overlap, the intersecting portion is evaluated as: Overlap = Sum of individual subset sums − Total value of the whole.

Weighted Average

Used when combining groups with different item counts and averages. Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p

questions.question: The value of 50 - 7 × [ 2 + 5 × { 16 - 2 ( 6 - 5 ) × 8} ÷ 31] is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Solve brackets from inside out: (6 − 5) = 1.

Simplify curly braces: {16 − 2 × 1 × 8} = 16 − 16 = 0.

Simplify square brackets: [2 + 5 × 0 ÷ 31] = 2 + 0 = 2.

Final Step: 50 − 7 × 2 = 50 − 14 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 50 − 7 × [2 + 5 × {16 − 2(6 − 5) × 8} ÷ 31]

**Formula Used:** BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 50 − 7 × [2 + 5 × {16 − 2(1) × 8} ÷ 31]

⇒ 50 − 7 × [2 + 5 × {16 − 16} ÷ 31]

⇒ 50 − 7 × [2 + 5 × 0 ÷ 31]

⇒ 50 − 7 × [2 + 0]

⇒ 50 − 14

⇒ 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Determines the sequence of operations: Brackets → Orders → Division/Multiplication → Addition/Subtraction.

Order of Brackets

Always solve in this order: Parentheses (), then Braces {}, and finally Square Brackets [].

Multiplication and Division Priority

Division and Multiplication carry equal priority and should be performed from left to right as they appear in the expression.</p

questions.question: A man sold an article for ₹217, there by gaining 8.5%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Fraction equivalent of 8.5% = 8.5 ÷ 100 = 17 ÷ 200

Let Cost Price (CP) = 200 units, then Gain = 17 units.

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Gain = 200 + 17 = 217 units.

Given 217 units = ₹217 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹1

Cost Price = 200 units = 200 × 1 = ₹200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of the article = ₹217

⇒ Gain percentage = 8.5%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 + Gain%)] × SP

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = ?
 (100%)
 
 
 SP = ₹217
 (108.5%)

 

 + 8.5% Gain
 
 CP = (217 ÷ 108.5) × 100 = ₹200

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [100 ÷ (100 + 8.5)] × 217

⇒ CP = (100 ÷ 108.5) × 217

⇒ CP = (1000 ÷ 1085) × 217

⇒ CP = (200 ÷ 217) × 217

⇒ CP = 200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage Formula

When an article is sold below its cost price, the loss percentage is calculated as: Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of the item. The effective Selling Price is determined by: SP = MP × [1 − (Discount% ÷ 100)].

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are applied, the equivalent single discount percentage is given by: [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

questions.question: A man goes to Ahmedabad from Kolkata at a speed of 4km/hr and returns to Kolkata at speed of 12km/hr, through same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance covered is equal in both directions, the formula for average speed is (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Here, the onward speed S₁ = 4 km/hr and return speed S₂ = 12 km/hr

Average speed = (2 × 4 × 12) ÷ (4 + 12)

⇒ Average speed = 96 ÷ 16 = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 Kolkata
 Ahmedabad

 
• 
 Distance = D

 
• 
 

 Onward Speed = 4 km/hr

 
• 
 

 Return Speed = 12 km/hr

**Given:**

Speed from Kolkata to Ahmedabad = 4 km/hr

Speed from Ahmedabad to Kolkata = 12 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

Let the distance between Kolkata and Ahmedabad be D km.

⇒ Total distance for the entire journey = D + D = 2D km

⇒ Time taken for onward journey = D ÷ 4 hours

⇒ Time taken for return journey = D ÷ 12 hours

⇒ Total time taken = (D ÷ 4) + (D ÷ 12)

⇒ Total time taken = (3D + D) ÷ 12 = 4D ÷ 12 = D ÷ 3 hours

⇒ Average speed = 2D ÷ (D ÷ 3)

⇒ Average speed = 2 × 3 = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

When a person travels two equal distances at speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed is given directly by the harmonic mean of the speeds: (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

When a person covers three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is (3xyz) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Average Speed for Unequal Distances

For journey segments of differing distances, always use the fundamental formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.
</p

questions.question: What is the single per cent discount equivalent to two successive discounts of 18.5% and 11.5%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the single equivalent discount is given by: **x + y − (x × y) / 100**

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 18.5 + 11.5 − (18.5 × 11.5) / 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 30 − 212.75 / 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 30 − 2.1275 = 27.8725%

**∴ The correct answer is 27.8725%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First discount (D₁) = 18.5%

Second discount (D₂) = 11.5%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Marked Price (MP) = 100

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − D₁ / 100) × (1 − D₂ / 100)

⇒ SP = 100 × (1 − 18.5 / 100) × (1 − 11.5 / 100)

⇒ SP = 100 × (81.5 / 100) × (88.5 / 100)

⇒ SP = (81.5 × 88.5) / 100

*Using algebraic identity (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²:*

⇒ SP = [(85 − 3.5) × (85 + 3.5)] / 100

⇒ SP = (7225 − 12.25) / 100

questions.question: What will be difference in population 3 years ago and 2 years ago of a town, whose current population is 110000 and which is increasing at a rate of 25% every year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of increase = 25% = 1/4 ⇒ Yearly multiplying factor = 5/4.

Let population 3 years ago be 64x (as 4³ = 64 to avoid fractions).

Population values ⇒ 3 yrs ago = 64x, 2 yrs ago = 64x × (5/4) = 80x, Present = 64x × (5/4)³ = 125x.

Present population = 125x = 110000 ⇒ x = 880.

Required difference (2 yrs ago − 3 yrs ago) = 80x − 64x = 16x.

Difference = 16 × 880 = 14080.

**∴ The correct answer is 14080.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present population = 110000

Rate of increase (R) = 25%

**Formula Used:**

P = P₀ × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Present population = Population 2 years ago × (1 + 25/100)²

⇒ 110000 = Population 2 years ago × (5/4) × (5/4)

⇒ Population 2 years ago = 110000 × (16/25) = 70400

⇒ Present population = Population 3 years ago × (1 + 25/100)³

Successive Population Change

When population changes successively by R₁%, R₂%, etc., the final population is calculated as P = P₀ × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100).

Ratio Method for Constant Rate

If the rate of percentage increase is equivalent to fraction a/b, the ratio of initial to final quantity after 'n' years translates directly to bⁿ : (b+a)ⁿ.

Population Decrease / Depreciation

For a constant decrease rate of R% annually, the retained value after 'n' years is strictly defined by P = P₀ × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.
</p

questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹42 and compound interest is ₹43, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is simply the interest earned on the 1st year's simple interest.

1st year's SI = ₹42 ÷ 2 = ₹21.

Difference = ₹43 − ₹42 = ₹1 (This is the interest earned on ₹21 in the 2nd year).

Rate (R) = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100 = (1 ÷ 21) × 100%.

Principal = (1st year's SI × 100) ÷ R = (21 × 100) ÷ (100/21) = 21 × 21 = ₹441.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹441.**

SI for 2 years = ₹42

CI for 2 years = ₹43

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI is the same for every year, so 1st year's SI = 42 ÷ 2 = ₹21

⇒ CI for the 2nd year = Total CI − 1st year's SI = 43 − 21 = ₹22

⇒ Extra interest generated in the 2nd year = CI for 2nd year − SI for 2nd year = 22 − 21 = ₹1

⇒ This ₹1 is the simple interest calculated on the 1st year's SI (₹21) for a period of 1 year.

⇒ Rate (R) = (100 × Interest) ÷ (Principal × Time)

⇒ R = (100 × 1) ÷ (21 × 1) = 100/21%

⇒ Now, substitute R into the SI formula for the 1st year:

⇒ 21 = (P × (100/21) × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 21 = P ÷ 21

⇒ P = 21 × 21

⇒ P = ₹441

**∴ The correct answer is ₹441.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI (2 Years)

The formula is Diff = P × (R/100)². It strictly represents the interest generated on the first year's simple interest.

Difference between CI and SI (3 Years)

The formula is Diff = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100). This formula helps bypass lengthy calculations for 3-year differences.

Uniformity of Simple Interest

Simple Interest (SI) is calculated only on the original principal. Therefore, the interest earned remains constant for every year of the investment period.

questions.question: The price (per litre) of petrol increases by 50%. By what percent should its consumption be reduced such that the expenditure on it increases by 11% only?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial Expenditure = 100

Due to a 50% price increase, expenditure to maintain the same consumption = 150

Allowed expenditure is only 11% higher ⇒ Target Expenditure = 111

Required reduction in consumption = [(150 − 111) ÷ 150] × 100

⇒ Reduction % = (39 ÷ 150) × 100 = 26%

**∴ The correct answer is 26%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase in the price of petrol = 50%

Allowed percentage increase in expenditure = 11%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

 
 100

 150
 Required Exp.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price of petrol be 100/litre and initial consumption be 100 litres.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = Price × Consumption = 100 × 100 = 10000 units.

⇒ New Price = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150/litre.

⇒ Target Expenditure = 10000 + 11% of 10000 = 11100 units.

⇒ Target Expenditure = New Price × New Consumption

⇒ 11100 = 150 × New Consumption

⇒ New Consumption = 11100 ÷ 150 = 74 litres.

⇒ Reduction in consumption = Initial Consumption − New Consumption = 100 − 74 = 26 litres.

⇒ Percentage reduction = (26 ÷ 100) × 100 = 26%.

**∴ The correct answer is 26%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Expenditure Rule

When expenditure remains constant, price and consumption are inversely proportional: P₁ × C₁ = P₂ × C₂.

Percentage Change Formula

Change % = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100.

Successive Percentage Change

The net percentage change for two successive changes of a% and b% is given by the formula: (a + b + ab/100)%.

questions.question: The average of 19 consecutive natural numbers is 41. What is the smallest number among these numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an odd number of consecutive integers, the average is exactly the middle term.

Middle term position = (19 + 1) ÷ 2 = 10th term.

Since the 10th term is 41, we move backward 9 steps to find the 1st term.

Smallest term = 41 − 9 = 32.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of consecutive natural numbers (n) = 19

Average of these numbers = 41

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of terms ÷ Total number of terms

Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n + 1) ÷ 2

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Smallest
 32
 
 Average (Middle)
 41
 
 Largest
 50

 
 

 

 −9 steps
 
 

 

 +9 steps

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the 19 consecutive natural numbers be x, x + 1, x + 2, ..., x + 18

⇒ Total sum = 19x + (0 + 1 + 2 + ... + 18)

⇒ Total sum = 19x + [18 × 19 ÷ 2]

⇒ Total sum = 19x + 171

⇒ Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of terms

⇒ 41 = (19x + 171) ÷ 19

⇒ 41 = x + 9

⇒ x = 41 − 9

⇒ x = 32

⇒ The smallest number is x = 32.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Consecutive Numbers

If n is an odd number, the average of n consecutive integers is always exactly the middle term, which is located at the (n + 1)÷2 th position.

Average of Arithmetic Progression

The average of any sequence forming an arithmetic progression (like consecutive numbers, even numbers, or odd numbers) is given by (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

Largest Number Shortcut

For n consecutive integers with a known average A, the largest number in the series can be directly computed as A + (n − 1)÷2.
</p

questions.question: The simple interest on a principal amount (in ₹) is ₹576 for a period of 3 years at the rate of 6% per annum. The principal amount (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of Simple Interest for 3 years = 6% × 3 = 18%.

According to the question, 18% of Principal = ₹576.

1% of Principal = 576 ÷ 18 = ₹32.

100% of Principal = 32 × 100 = ₹3200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹576

Rate of Interest (R) = 6% per annum

Time Period (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

where P is the Principal amount.

 
 Principal (P)
 ? = ₹3200
 
 
 Simple Interest
 ₹576
 
 

 

 
 
 Time = 3 Yrs
 Rate = 6% p.a.
 
 Effective Rate = 18% of Principal = ₹576

**Calculations:**

⇒ 576 = (P × 6 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 576 = (P × 18) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (576 × 100) ÷ 18

⇒ P = 32 × 100

⇒ P = 3200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) returned after the period is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest. The formula is A = P(1 + RT/100).

Compound Interest (CI)

In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods. The formula is A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Difference Between SI and CI

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on the same principal is calculated directly using the formula: Difference = P(R/100)².

questions.question: Ketan bought a shirt and sold it to Mahesh at a profit of 5%. Mahesh sold it to David at a loss of 24%. If David paid ₹3990, then the cost price (in ₹) of the shirt Ketan bought is

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the fractional multiplier method for successive profit and loss:

Initial CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 × (100 − L%) ÷ 100 = Final SP

⇒ CP × 105/100 × 76/100 = 3990

⇒ CP × 21/20 × 19/25 = 3990

⇒ CP × 399/500 = 3990

⇒ CP = 3990 × 500 ÷ 399 = 5000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit percentage of Ketan = 5%

Loss percentage of Mahesh = 24%

Price paid by David = ₹3990

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 − Loss% ÷ 100)
